reviewed_loopback_source_observations.scope: Static official CLI 1.9.1 source observation for FrontendIP wiring; the contract still requires runtime inspection of actual owned listener addresses.

decision: approved_for_h1_test_authoring_and_separately_reviewed_pre_gate; runtime/test execution still requires the specified pre-gate source review

findings.topic: Five-case inventory and independent expected values
findings.evidence: The four pytest function IDs expand to exactly five collected cases because the absent and truncated binary case has two parameters. The contract pins package versions, fixed verifier errors, synthetic workflow result/history, workflow/run ID equality, retention greater than 3600 seconds, and typed duplicate-start failures. The expected values are literal and are not derived from the implementation under test.

findings.topic: CLI provenance and loopback configuration basis
findings.evidence: The contract pins the CLI archive and binary hashes and includes the reviewed official 1.9.1 source observations that FrontendIP is applied to frontend/internal RPC BindOnIP and the metrics listener. It explicitly treats this as a configuration basis, not runtime proof or source-to-binary attestation, and separately requires the actual owned TCP listener addresses to be inspected and rejected if any are non-loopback. It disables ambient config/env discovery and supplies a private env file containing exactly the empty JSON object {}.

The readiness path calls Client.connect and DescribeNamespaceRequest for the default namespace, converts the reported workflow_execution_retention_ttl to seconds, and checks it is strictly greater than 3600 before starting. The running duplicate uses FAIL conflict policy; the closed duplicate uses REJECT_DUPLICATE reuse policy. Each must raise the pinned WorkflowAlreadyStartedError and preserve the original run identity/history.

The test blocks a deterministic synthetic workflow on a signal, records workflow/run IDs and an ordered history prefix, then stops and reaps the first CLI server, worker and client. It restarts the exact CLI against the same private SQLite file and ports, creates fresh client and worker processes, and requires the same run ID and prior history prefix before signaling the already-running execution. It prohibits a second start after restart and verifies the completed-ID duplicate is rejected.

findings.topic: Timeouts, process ownership and evidence handling
findings.evidence: Ordinary tests are limited to 30 seconds and the single multi-process integration has a declared 240-second exception within the unchanged 300-second Python phase. Startup, RPC, worker readiness, query, graceful shutdown and owned cleanup have individual limits. Cleanup checks saved PID/start-time identities and avoids name-based process killing. Raw history/logs remain private; publication is sanitized.

The exact contract continues to authorize only H1 tool qualification after the separate source pre-gate review. It does not claim business workflow implementation or acceptance of AT-05, AT-16, AT-29, AT-09, or original AT-01 through AT-32.

conditions: Before runtime execution, the independent pre-gate review must compare frozen launcher, runner, tests and fixture hashes with this exact contract and confirm the private installation still matches the artifact pins.
The actual server process must expose only loopback listeners. The source observation cannot substitute for that runtime socket assertion.
Any CLI/SDK behavior, typed error, retention, listener or history discrepancy is a review finding; do not relax the oracle to match observed behavior.
Use a new private attempt directory and store; only the two restart phases may reuse that one store. Keep raw logs and full history private.

acceptance_boundary.H1: not accepted; requires frozen implementation, test execution, owned-process cleanup proof and independent evidence audit
